system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Kubernetes
G2: AWS/GCP
G3: LLM fine-tuning or LLMs in production
G4: computer vision
G5: completed PhD

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Translating 'Doktorandica (u tijeku)' as holding a PhD or adding 'Dr.'
T2: Inventing LLM/RAG production experience from the weekend demo
T3: Adding Kubernetes, AWS, MLOps platforms (Kubeflow, SageMaker) because ML ads list them
T4: Mistranslating employer or degree (Mag. ing. comp. is a master's degree)
T5: Writing the English output with Croatian section headings or leaving Croatian text untranslated
T6: Old Croatian cover letter is addressed to her current employer

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Machine Learning Engineer | NLP and Document AI
Professional Summary
Machine learning engineer with production experience in text classification, named entity recognition
and model monitoring on Azure. Fine-tuned transformer models for document processing at
approximately 15,000 documents per day. Earlier banking experience includes customer complaint
classification and churn prediction. Doctoral research focuses on named entity recognition in Croatian
legal texts.
Technical Skills
• Languages and data: Python, SQL, pandas, PostgreSQL, Oracle SQL.
• NLP and model development: PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, spaCy, scikit-learn, fastText,
TF-IDF, XLM-R, BERTic.
• Production serving and MLOps: FastAPI, Docker, Azure App Service, Azure ML, Azure
Functions, MLflow, Evidently.
• Text datasets and retrieval: Label Studio, annotation guidelines, sentence-transformers, FAISS;
RAG prototype experience.
Professional Experience
ML Engineer | Slavonica Document AI | 2023-Present
• Develop document classification and named entity recognition models for Croatian public
administration documents.
• Fine-tuned XLM-R base to classify OCR-processed invoices, contracts and decisions into 23
classes, achieving 94% accuracy and macro F1 of 0.91.
• Served the classifier through FastAPI in Docker on Azure App Service, processing approximately
15,000 documents per day.
• Fine-tuned BERTic to identify persons, organisations, OIB numbers, addresses and legal references
in Croatian administrative text.
• Built an annotated dataset of 4,000 documents with annotation guidelines and two annotators,
achieving inter-annotator kappa of 0.87. This work was published at a regional workshop in 2024.
• Implemented weekly model drift reporting on input text length, vocabulary and predicted class
distribution, with alerts when PSI exceeded 0.2, using Python, Evidently, Azure Functions and
PostgreSQL.
• Detected a silent client-side OCR change that reduced accuracy by 9 percentage points; the issue
was fixed within a week.
Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka | 2021-2023
• Developed models for customer churn prediction and customer complaint classification.
• Built an 11-topic complaint classifier using a TF-IDF and logistic regression baseline, followed by
fastText, for weekly reporting to customer service management.
• Used scikit-learn, pandas and Oracle SQL for complaint classification work.
Selected Personal Project
Retrieval-augmented Question Answering Demo | 2025
• Built a weekend RAG prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using sentence
embeddings, FAISS and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
• Personal prototype only; assessed through manual checks, not deployed to production.
Education
Doctoral studies, in progress | Sveučilište Drava
Expected completion: 2027
Research topic: Named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts.
Certification
Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024
Teaching and Languages
• Delivered a 90-minute guest lecture at an NLP summer school in 2025.
• English: used daily in meetings with a client from Slovenia.

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel
Application: Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI
Quillstone Payments
Dear Hiring Team,
Your work on merchant questions, ticket routing and support-agent assistance connects
directly with my experience in production NLP and customer complaint classification. As an
ML Engineer at Slavonica Document AI, I develop and serve models for Croatian public
administration documents. Previously, at Baranjska kreditna banka, I built complaint
classifiers used for weekly customer service reporting. I would bring both experiences to
Quillstone Payments’ Customer Operations AI team.
At Slavonica, I fine-tuned XLM-R for 23 document classes, achieving 94% accuracy and macro
F1 of 0.91, and served it through FastAPI and Docker on Azure App Service at approximately
15,000 documents per day. My work also covers production monitoring: a weekly drift report
detected a silent OCR change at a client that reduced accuracy by 9 percentage points, and
the issue was fixed within a week. This experience is directly relevant to your requirement to
build, deploy and operate ML systems, rather than stop at a successful prototype.
Dataset quality and model evaluation are also central to my work. For Croatian named entity
recognition, I built a 4,000-document annotated dataset with guidelines and two annotators,
achieving inter-annotator kappa of 0.87, and fine-tuned BERTic. My toolkit includes Python,
PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, MLflow and Azure ML, supported by my Azure AI
Engineer Associate certification. I have also explored retrieval-augmented question answering
over Croatian laws in a personal prototype using sentence embeddings, FAISS and an
open-weight LLM API; this was exploratory work, not a production assistant.
Quillstone’s focus on helping merchants get support quickly offers a clear application for my
background in extracting useful information from text. Your emphasis on service ownership
also aligns with the deployment and monitoring work I have undertaken. I would welcome a
conversation about how my production NLP experience and customer-service classification
background could contribute to your team.
Kind regards,
Petra Zlatarić-Novosel

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
